## WGSmart v1.0.5

**Smart Rules was quietly disarming your kill switch and shipping other people's Wi-Fi names as trusted defaults — both are fixed, and automation is rebuilt on a model that can no longer produce either mistake.**

### 🐞 Fixed
- **"Disconnect when Wi-Fi Off" was silently removing the kill-switch firewall.** It tore every active tunnel down on any brief network drop (sleep/wake, AP roam), and the daemon removes the pf firewall once no tunnel is active — so a two-second blip could leave the machine online with neither a tunnel nor a firewall, while Settings still showed the kill switch on. This rule is now deleted; a dropped link never disconnects anything on its own.
- **The default trusted-network list shipped as the developer's own Wi-Fi names.** Every fresh install trusted four specific networks nobody had chosen, published in a public binary — and since a trusted network makes the VPN stand down, those names could disarm any install that had never touched the setting. Existing installs are cleared automatically **only if the list still matches exactly those four defaults**; anything you edited yourself is left alone.
- **"Launch at Login" did nothing.** The toggle existed but was never wired to the system — so after a reboot, Smart Rules automation was not running at all, silently, while the app still reported it active. It now registers a real macOS login item.
- **"Engine Active" could say Active while nothing was happening**, or the reverse. Status now reflects whether any rule can actually act, not one flag out of several.

### ✨ New
- **Per-tunnel activation rules**, replacing three global switches with one setting per tunnel. Each tunnel can connect on Wi-Fi and/or Ethernet, on *any* network, *only* specific ones, or *every network except* the ones you trust — and choose whether it disconnects elsewhere or is simply left alone.
- **Wired networks are covered.** Automation previously only recognized Wi-Fi, so a wired office or hotel connection got no protection at all.
- **Two tunnels can now activate on the same network at once** — a shape a single "default tunnel" could never express.
- Your existing settings carry over automatically: whatever a tunnel did before, it does the same thing under the new model — no reconfiguration needed.

### 🛠️ Improved
- The Smart Rules screen now shows, per tunnel, exactly why it will or won't activate on the network you're on, instead of a set of switches you had to interpret yourself.
- Manually starting or stopping a tunnel is now respected until the network changes — automation no longer immediately undoes something you just did by hand.

---

### Install
1. Download **`WGSmart-1.0.5.pkg`** below.
2. Double-click to install WGSmart.app + the background daemon.
3. First launch: right-click ▸ **Open** (until notarized).

**Requirements:** macOS on Apple Silicon · administrator access.
